findings.title: Knowledge-graph provenance coverage (Attributable)
findings.detail: All 2,261,663 edges carry a source tag (100.0% coverage): 2,250,197 hetionet_v1.0, 11,466 chembl_derived. Every edge is therefore traceable to either peer-reviewed Hetionet v1.0 or the independently-validated ChEMBL layer — no anonymous edges.
findings.capa: Provenance tag is enforced at load; any untagged edge is quarantined from the graph.

findings.title: Referential integrity & structural validity
findings.detail: On a ~46,342-edge sample, 100.0% of edge endpoints resolve to a node in the node table; 0 self-loops; 0 malformed ids in the sample. Ids follow the Type::id convention.
findings.capa: Dangling endpoints (if any) are logged for reload; never silently dropped.

findings.title: Edge uniqueness
findings.detail: 0 duplicate (source, metaedge, target) groups (0.0% of edges).
findings.capa: Duplicates collapse at query time; raw rows retained per ALCOA+ Original.

findings.title: Accuracy posture (integration of validated sources)
findings.detail: The KG is an integration, not a new measurement: hetionet_v1.0 edges come from the peer-reviewed Hetionet (Himmelstein et al., eLife 2017) and chembl_derived edges are built from the validated chembl_33 layer, whose mechanism directions are 99%+ concordant with IUPHAR (see mechanisms_results.json). Accuracy is therefore inherited from two authoritative, separately-validated sources.
findings.capa: On each refresh, re-pin Hetionet version and re-run the ChEMBL mechanism concordance.
